hook: Deuterium-labeled amino acids let Raman microscopy image protein condensates in live cells without tags.
summary: Cells fed deuterated tyrosine and arginine build them into proteins, and stimulated Raman microscopy then shows FUS condensates, linked to ALS, without bulky fluorescent tags. Pulse-chase imaging shows translation stalls in condensates under stress, and tyrosine phosphorylation is seen through a Raman shift. The work is in cultured cells and centers on FUS.
title: Specific Amino Acid Imaging of Protein Condensates in Live Cells by Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
